question: How do tracing, evaluations, and Signals fit together?

observer.firstAnswerText:
Tracing records what your app or agent actually did [S5, S2]. Evaluations test your app against a fixed set of examples so you can compare changes [S3]. Signals automatically score and tag your agent's conversations so you can find problems in production [S1].

1. Tracing: see what happened

If you build multi-turn agents, the Weave SDK for Agents records the agent, its conversations, each turn (one user–agent exchange), the LLM calls inside a turn, and the tool calls they trigger. You can view these in the Agents tab [S5, S4].
Weave is built on OpenTelemetry, an open tracing standard. Each turn, LLM call and tool call creates a span, which is a record of one operation [S5].
If your app calls LLMs directly, provider and framework integrations record each LLM call and pipeline step as a Weave Call, shown in the Traces view [S2].

2. Evaluations: measure against repeatable tests

An Evaluation object combines a dataset of test examples with one or more scoring functions. You run it against a Model or a function with .evaluate(), and each run gives a measurement [S3].
Use evaluations to compare versions over time and catch regressions (cases where a change makes results worse) [S3].

3. Signals: watch quality in production

In the Agents view, the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. For example, it can score response quality, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content [S1].
A rating is a score from 0.0 to 1.0, and tags are labels such as "user-frustration." Both are attached to matching spans, which come from your agent traces [S4, S5].
Scoring uses an LLM judge by default. You can use an HTTP endpoint you host instead [S1].

How they connect (my reading of the docs): Signals depend on agent tracing because they score traced conversations [S1, S4, S5]. Evaluations are a separate workflow: they score curated examples during development [S3]. In practice, Signals show you problems in real traffic, and evaluations let you test fixes on repeatable examples.
